e: Switzerland pledges about $2 million for humanitarian aid in Yemen.

The head of the internationally recognized Presidential Leadership Council (PLC), Rashad al-Alimi, formally announces the start of a full-scale military counteroffensive from Saudi Arabia to reclaiming all remaining Houthi-controlled territories. The Saudi-led coalition promises to back the offensive.
Al-Masirah announces that Saudi Arabia conducted 24 attacks on Sanaa. Government forces state that they struck "legitimate vital military targets in Sanaa”.
The Saba News Agency reports Saudi attacks in Sanaa.
The Yemeni Air Force announces that it conducted 20 strikes on Houthi targets in Taiz Governorate.
The Houthis state that Saudi Arabia conducted 94 attacks in parts of Yemen under their governance in the last day.
Houthi media declares that the Saudi Arabian Armed Forces struck Sanaa for the first time in years.

The Houthi-run health ministry states that an attack on a market in the Mawiya junction of Taiz Governorate killed seven people and wounded 40 others, including children. The government states that its targets were a Houthi military camp and vehicles at the same area.
President Rashad al-Alimi calles on Yemenis to join the armed forces against the Houthis and promises a general amnesty for Houthi fighters and affiliates who leave the group beginning the next day.
The government claims to have thwarted a Houthi attack on a vital supply route to Aden.
Government soldiers claim that they captured Mount Qarfan in Taiz Governorate.
Saba News Agency announces that six civilians, including two children and a woman, were killed and eight others, including a child and a woman were wounded in Saudi attacks in Mokha.
Al-Masirah reports that Saudi attacks targeted three telecommunications towers in Taiz Governorate, while one civilian was killed and another wounded in attacks on Abs.
Al-Masirah reports that government attacks in Taiz Governorate killed three children and wounded several others.
The Houthis state that they downed a Saudi F15 over Marib Governorate.
The Houthis complete their takeover of the Bab el-Mandeb region by recapturing Perim Island, opening a new front in the 2026 Iran war.
The Houthis complete their seizure of the entire Red Sea coast by recapturing the Hanish Islands.

The Houthis launch missile and drone attacks on civilian, economic and military facilities in Abha, Jizan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, wounding 73 people, including women and children, and igniting fires at oil facilities and utilities in southern Saudi Arabia.
Government forces launch a counteroffensive against the Houthis, with the goal of recapturing Sanaa.
Government forces state that they retook Hays district.
The Houthis launch a general offensive in coastal regions for control of the Bab-el-Mandeb, resulting in significant losses for its forces as well as government forces.
Eight soldiers are killed and 12 others are injured in a Houthi attack in Marib Governorate. The government states that a Houthi attack on Marib killed two civilians.
At least 58 government soldiers are killed in Houthi attacks. Saudi Arabia later says that a Houthi missile attack in Najran Province injured 11 civilians.
The Yemeni Air Force conducts strikes on Houthi missile and drone firing sites in Marib and Al-Jawf Governorate.
Saudi Arabia carries out attacks on Hudaydah Port and facilities owned by the state telecommunications corporation in Hodeidah and Kamaran.
The Houthis declare a blockade of Saudi Arabian ports and ships in the Bab-el-Mandeb.

The defense ministry announces that it struck Sanaa International Airport's runway to ‌prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing. The Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of conducting the attack. The Houthis later fire missiles towards Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia.
Houthis kill 16 soldiers belonging to the internationally-recognised government in an attack in Hays district. Pro-government soldiers reportedly kill 50 Houthi fighters.
Twelve soldiers are killed in an explosion at a military base run by the Southern Giants Brigades in Aden.
The Houthi-controlled Specialized Criminal Court in Sanaa sentences 19 people to death for collaborating with the Saudi-led coalition.
The Houthis and the PLC agree to release 1,680 detainees as part of a prisoner exchange.
The Houthis join the 2026 Iran war, conducting a ballistic missile attack towards Israel and triggering air raid sirens in Beersheba.
Demonstrators in Sanaa rally in solitary with Iran and Lebanon amidst the conflict.
Protesters linked to the STC attempt to storm the gate of the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, leaving one person dead and 11 others injured.
Protesters linked to the STC attack a government building in Ataq, leaving five people dead.
The PLC appoints a new cabinet under prime minister Zindani.
Famine in Yemen: The World Food Programme ceases operations in Houthi-controlled territories following harassment from the Houthis.
The Houthis seize equipment and vehicles from six United Nations offices in Sanaa.
Five people are killed in a car bombing in Ja’awla, north of Aden targeting a convoy carrying Hamdi Shukri, a commander of the Southern Giants Brigades.
